about.title: About Me
about.name: Alina
about.bio1: Lovely to meet you — I'm Alina, and my story with horses began long before I ever picked up a camera. As a former rider, I know the racing pulse before a round, the quiet bond with the horse and the drive for perfection in every movement.
about.bio2: My military service put riding on hold for a while, but it only sharpened my need to stay connected to this world another way. Today I'm building Lens Dance from the angle I always looked for as a rider: clean, precise, uncompromising photography.
about.quote: "I'm not here to document an event, but to capture a moment in time — a feeling and a memory that last a lifetime"
about.philosophy: My focus is creativity, attention to the smallest details and a clean style — the kind that changes what a "simple photo" means and turns it into a work of art.

qa.q: What do you most love to photograph?
qa.a: Show jumping — the moment between the horse and the fence is the purest there is. But also horse portraits: when they look straight at you, words become unnecessary.

qa.q: What makes you different as an equestrian photographer?
qa.a: My background as a rider. I know the moment before it happens — I know when the horse is about to jump, when the rider locks in, and where the magic is.
Yes, I work across Israel and Europe. Every competition abroad is a new adventure — another language, another climate — but the horses are always the same horses.

contact.agreement:
Terms for ordering photos/videos from equestrian competitions

(This is a translation for convenience. The Hebrew version is the binding one.)

1. General:
This service offers photography and/or video of equestrian events, and delivery of the results to the client.
By ordering the service, the client agrees to the terms set out below.

2. Placing an order:
Photography services are booked in advance.
Please make sure the client's details, the horse's and rider's details, and the competition and class details are accurate and clearly communicated.

3. Delivery times:
Standard delivery: photos and/or videos are sent to the client within 10 business days from the end of the competition.
Delivery during an emergency: in the event of a national emergency (such as war, a military operation or a natural disaster) delivery may take longer. Delivery resumes once the emergency ends, plus a reasonable amount of time for processing. The client will be updated about any such change as soon as possible.

4. Quality and content:
The photography is done professionally, but a perfect shot of every single moment cannot be guaranteed.
The delivered files receive basic editing and enhancement (such as colour and lighting correction) at the photographer's discretion.

5. Use of the results:
The client may use the photos and/or videos for personal use only, including posting them on social media.
Credit must be given to the photographer when posting (for example a tag or a mention).
Publication by the photographer: with the client's approval, the photographer may use photos and/or videos in which the client appears for self-promotion on social media or on the photographer's website.
The client's name should be mentioned when publishing, in order to credit them.
Commercial use of the results is prohibited without explicit prior approval.
Once the client approves publication of their photos, the photographer may use them on social media and on the website.

6. Payment:
Payment details are agreed with the client before the shoot. Securing the booking requires a 40% deposit of the package price; the balance is due on delivery.
Payment constitutes the client's final acceptance of these terms.
If the client wishes to cancel the order before the competition (10 hours before the class starts), they receive a full refund.
If a deposit was paid and the competition was cancelled for any reason, the deposit is refunded in full.
If the client requests a refund after receiving the photos/videos, no refund is given. A request can be submitted for the case to be reviewed on its merits, and the decision is at the photographer's discretion.
If a refund is approved, the client may not use the photos they received without the photographer's consent.

7. Conduct and mutual respect:
The service is provided on a basis of mutual respect and pleasant communication.
If a client behaves disrespectfully or offensively, the photographer reserves the right to decline to provide services to that client in the future.

8. Acceptance:
Payment constitutes the client's final acceptance of these terms.

faq.title: Common questions
faq.subtitle: What riders ask before their first shoot. If yours isn't here, message me — I answer faster than this page updates.
faq.stillStuck: Still not sure about something? Send me a message on WhatsApp. There is no question too small, and I would rather answer it now than on the morning of the competition.

items.q: Do I have to sign up before the competition?
items.a:
Yes — riders who haven't signed up aren't photographed. I plan where I stand and when I shoot around the list of riders I have, so if you aren't on it I won't know to look for you.

Sign up through the form. It takes two minutes and asks for your class, your horse and how to reach you.

items.q: How should I prepare for a personal session?
items.a:
My sessions run at an easy, unhurried pace, so that both you and your horse enjoy the day. To arrive as prepared as possible, get your horse ready as you would for a competition — a good groom, and clean, polished tack. As for clothes, simply wear what you feel comfortable in; there is a separate question below devoted to outfits.

On the day, bring treats your horse likes to keep him cooperative, along with wet wipes and a brush for a last touch-up right before we start. One more golden tip: bring a friend or someone from the family. An extra pair of hands can sort out small details, hold equipment, and catch your horse's attention at exactly the right moment to get those ears forward. And if you have ideas of your own, or particular shots you have been dreaming of, tell me in advance and we will work them into the session.

I recommend choosing an outfit you feel comfortable in, in a colour that flatters your horse's coat and tack. Colour is the one thing worth planning in advance: between the tack and the outfit, aim for no more than one stand-out colour — a white saddle pad with a red top, for instance, works beautifully. Keep everything else in quiet, neutral tones: grey, black, navy or cream.

On overcast days, strong, bold colours work better. Either way, bring two or three options with you on the day so we can decide together, on the spot, what suits the light and the location best. (The two-hour session allows up to three outfits — a riding look and a casual one, say — while the one-hour session is a single outfit.)

Fabrics with an interesting texture — knits, denim, leather — and a few delicate accessories such as a hat or some jewellery can add a great deal of character to the photographs.

items.q: Anything different for the black & white session?
items.a:
A little, yes. That session is shot dark and close, so the setup matters more than usual.

  • Take the reins off and clip a lead rope to the bridle — you keep control of your horse, and the rope comes out in editing.
  • Turn the lights off and find a clean stretch of aisle near an open door. The floor shows up in some frames.
  • Bring a friend. Keeping a horse's ears forward for twenty minutes is a two-person job.

It's the shortest session I offer and the slowest to edit — five finished portraits, each one worked properly.

items.q: How do I pay, and what is the deposit?
items.a:
40% of the package price up front holds your date; the balance is due on delivery. The deposit is what makes travelling to a shoot possible at all, which is why I ask for it rather than taking bookings on trust.

Payment by Bit, Paybox, cash or bank transfer. For clients outside Israel, PayPal as well. We agree the details before the shoot, and paying the deposit is what confirms the booking.

items.q: What if I need to cancel?
items.a:
Cancel more than 10 hours before the competition and the deposit comes back to you, no questions asked.

Cancel inside 10 hours, or don't turn up, and the deposit isn't refunded — by that point the travel is booked and the day is held for you.

Once the photos have been delivered there's no refund. You've seen exactly what you're paying for before the balance is due.

Within Israel, travel is included in the price you see.

For competitions abroad, travel is part of what we agree before booking — I'll tell you the number up front, and it never appears as a surprise line afterwards. Ask through the custom package button on the pricing page and I'll come back with a figure.

items.q: How and when do I get my photos?
items.a:
Through your own gallery on this site. Once the balance is paid I upload your photos there — sign in with the account you registered with and download them, one at a time or all at once.

Standard delivery is within 10 business days of the competition or session. If you'd rather not wait, see the next question.

Files arrive as full-quality JPGs. I don't send photos over WhatsApp or email — messaging apps compress images, and what reached you would be noticeably worse than what I shot.

Your photos within 48 hours instead of 10 business days, for half the price of the photo package.

Priority delivery is available at competitions only, not for personal sessions.

There are only a few places at each competition. A rush edit means a night's work, and there is a limit to how many of those fit into one weekend. You'll see how many places are left on the sign-up form, and the number drops as riders take them.

It depends which shoot.

From a personal session — yes. Those files come at print resolution, ready for a wall or an album.

From a competition — the files are ordinary JPGs, made for viewing and sharing. You can print them, but they weren't prepared specifically for print, so the result won't match a file made for the purpose.

Ordering prints through the site isn't something I offer yet. If it's something you'd want, tell me — it's on the list, and real demand is what moves it up.

items.q: Can I post the photos on social media?
items.a:
Please do — seeing your rounds turn up on my feed is one of the better parts of this job. Personal use, including social media, is exactly what the photos are for.

The one thing I ask is credit: tag @lens.dance29 on Instagram or @lensdance_photography on TikTok. Commercial use — a sponsor's post, an advert, anything being sold — needs to be agreed with me first.

items.q: Can I get more photos than the package includes?
items.a:
Yes. The number in each package is a floor, not a ceiling — it's what I commit to, not what I stop at.

If you see more in your gallery that you want, or you want more from a round than the package covers, message me and we'll agree a price for the extras. It's cheaper than booking a second package.

items.q: Do you shoot things that aren't on the pricing page?
items.a:
Often. Stable shoots, a whole team at one competition, a horse being sold, a foal's first week, an event that doesn't fit any of the boxes.

Use the custom package button on the pricing page — tell me what you have in mind and where, and I'll come back with a price. It reaches me on WhatsApp, so it usually gets an answer the same day.
